text: An AI drafts the reply. Then it stops. You decide whether it gets sent.
That pause matters. Meta's Muse can work across connected apps. But what are you actually handing over?
On September twenty ninth, Meta announced Muse for Small Business. This week's story is about doing the work, not just answering questions.
Picture a small shop. Customer questions in one place. Sales in another. Tomorrow's content still waiting. The owner is the connection between everything.
A chatbot might suggest a reply. You copy it, switch apps, check the order, and finish the job yourself.
An agent can take steps through connected tools. Meta lists integrations including Shopify, Canva, Slack, and business accounts on Instagram and Facebook.
Here is an illustrative workflow, not a recording of Muse. A customer asks about delivery. The task is to prepare a useful response.
The important part is context: which order, which delivery date, and what the shop has actually promised. A smooth sentence is not enough.
Meta says Muse can flag emails needing a response and write first drafts. That could move the owner from starting every task to reviewing prepared work.
But preparation is not permission. Meta says publishing, sending, and spending require your approval. The send button is still your decision.
Imagine the draft promises Friday, while the order says Monday. Approving that message quickly would turn a small error into a customer problem.
So the useful test is not whether the reply sounds human. It is whether the facts, recipient, and proposed action are right.
Meta says people choose connected apps and their access, and can disconnect a service. Start with the narrowest access that lets the task work.
Muse runs on a separate cloud computer. Meta describes a separate Sentinel checking outgoing actions. These are company safeguards, not proof that every task is safe.
Try one low-stakes job first: prepare a draft, compare it with the original, and count the corrections. Include checking time when judging any time saved.
The business announcement describes Muse as available in the United States and Canada. Check your own account's connectors and access before planning around it.
The opportunity is less switching between apps. The responsibility is more careful review. Would you trust it to draft, send, or spend? Tell us where your line is.
